name: corrections-010
prompt:
Create ORIGINAL FORMA fitness-manual illustrations. Exactly THREE columns TWO rows, SIX large separate panels, landscape 1536x1024. Pure white panels with generous margins, fully clothed varied adult athletes, charcoal/gray sportswear and equipment, small lime accents. Correct anatomy and plausible weight bearing. Full athlete and equipment fits entirely inside own panel. No letters, labels, logos, watermark. ONE clear accurate representative position per panel. Respect the mandatory correction, not a generic similar exercise. 

Row 1 column 1: Elbow to Knee. MANDATORY: Supine elbow-to-knee crunch: one ANKLE rests ON opposite bent KNEE in figure4; opposite elbow toward raised crossed knee.. Actual guide: Lie on the floor, crossing your right leg across your bent left knee. Clasp your hands behind your head, beginning with your shoulder blades on the ground. This will be your starting position.

Perform the motion by flexing the spine and rotating your torso to bring the left elbow to the right knee.

Return to the starting position and repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions before switching sides.

Row 1 column 2: Elevated Back Lunge. MANDATORY: Elevated reverse lunge: FRONT supporting FOOT entirely on raised step, REAR knee lowers behind toward floor with rear toes floor. No rear-knee platform.. Actual guide: Position a bar onto a rack at shoulder height loaded to an appropriate weight. Place a short, raised platform behind you.

Rack the bar onto your upper back, keeping your back arched and tight. Step onto your raised platform with both feet. This will be your starting position.

Begin by stepping backwards with one leg. Descend by flexing your hips and knees until your knee touches the floor.

Pause, and extend through the hips and knees to rise up, returning all the way to the starting position before alternating.

Row 1 column 3: Exercise Band Dorsiflexion. MANDATORY: Band DORSIFLEXION: seated with straight leg heel floor, band around FRONT of forefoot attached to LOW ANCHOR IN FRONT beyond toes. Pull toes toward shin resisting forward band tension. No holding band behind foot.. Actual guide: This exercise uses an exercise band. It targets the Soleus and Tibialis anterior.

Row 2 column 1: Extended Range One-Arm Kettlebell Floor Press. MANDATORY: One-arm kettlebell FLOOR press extended range: supine, pressing-side knee crosses MIDLINE over other leg, torso slightly rotates to side, single bell presses upward.. Actual guide: Lie on the floor and position a kettlebell for one arm to press. The kettlebell should be held by the handle. The leg on the same side that you are pressing should be bent, with the knee crossing over the midline of the body.

Press the kettlebell by extending the elbow and adducting the arm, pressing it above your body. Return to the starting position.

Row 2 column 2: External Rotation Stretch. MANDATORY: External rotation stretch seated with one knee raised and same ELBOW clearly RESTING ON THAT KNEE, forearm nearvertical and light dumbbell if guide.. Actual guide: 1. Sit with your feet pressed against each other, and one knee raised all the way out to the side of your body. 2. Place your elbow on your raised knee, bend it at 90 degrees, and point your hand directly forward, holding your barbell/dumbbell. 3. Keep your shoulder depressed and retracted, raise your hand until your forearm is vertical, as if you were about to wave at someone like a robot. 4. Lower your hand to the original position and repeat.

Row 2 column 3: Band external rotation. MANDATORY: Standing band external rotation: band anchored across body OPPOSITE the WORKING arm. Working elbow90 pinned side, working forearm rotates OUTWARD away from anchor.. Actual guide: Choke the band around a post. The band should be at the same height as your elbow. Stand with your left side to the band a couple of feet away.

Grasp the end of the band with your right hand, and keep your elbow pressed firmly to your side. We recommend you hold a pad or foam roll in place with your elbow to keep it firmly in position.

With your upper arm in position, your elbow should be flexed to 90 degrees with your hand reaching across the front of your torso. This will be your starting position.

Execute the movement by rotating your arm in a backhand motion, keeping your elbow in place.

Continue as far as you are able, pause, and then return to the starting position.
